newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel CPI-linked bonds end higher on June CPI.
newsitem.headline: Israel CPI-linked bonds end higher on June CPI.

text.p: Prices of Israel's CPI-linked bonds closed higher while unlinked bonds fell on Wednesday after publication on Tuesday of a higher than expected consumer price index, traders said.
Indices:
* Government bonds general: +0.10 pct to 109.84
* CPI-linked government bonds: +0.19 pct to 109.72
* Unlinked government bonds: -0.2 pct to 109.62
* Dollar-linked government bonds: +0.04 pct to 111.38
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: -0.02 pct to 107.84
Volume including Makams was an average 156 million shekels.

"There was no panic in the market today. I'd say the rise in the prices of CPI-linked bonds - mainly the short bonds - was in effect a technical rise, reflecting the difference between the CPI expectations and the real figure," said Danny Alt of Nesuah Trading and Investment.
Surplus demand for CPI-linked bonds was a high 438 million shekels. But prices of CPI-linked short bonds rose by about 0.5 while CPI-linked long bonds traded unchanged or slightly higher.

"Only tomorrow, after the CPI news has been digested, will we be able to see the real trends in the market," Alt said, adding that the high consumer price index did not reflect real inflation levels because of the undue influence of the dollar rise on housing prices.
"The basic trend of inflation has not really changed," he said.
The June CPI, published on Tuesday after the close of trading, rose by an unexpectedly large 1.1 percent after a rise of 0.5 percent in May.
Analysts' forecasts of June inflation were made difficult by the sharp depreciation of the Israeli shekel at the end of the month. Most economists were predicting inflation of 0.5 to 0.8 percent.

The inflation was due mainly to housing prices, which went up 2.4 percent, the Central Bureau of Statistics said. Housing prices, which are a major component of the index, accounted for 0.6 percentage points of the June increase.

Prices of unlinked bonds fell on Wednesday because of the high inflation figure, Alt said, and yields on one-year Makams were around 13 percent, up from 12.8 percent on Tuesday. "Unlinked bonds will stabilise around these levels," Alt said.
He predicted that yields on CPI-linked bonds would continue to ease, mainly because of the short supply of these bonds because the government was raising less debt.
"Yesterday's CPI quite significanly affected the market. No one expected such a high figure, and maybe some traders fear that this is a more significant change in inflation," said a trader.
She predicted the central bank would leave interest rates for August unchanged.
The Bank of Israel slashed its base lending rate in mid-June by 1.2 percentage points to an annualised 12.7 percent.
Dollar-linked bonds traded stable, traders said.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
($1 = 3.55 shekels)
- Shoshanna Solomon, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211
